card.law_is_about: Civil and criminal protection against digital violence.
card.they_want: Involve young people and adapt the law to minors’ needs.
card.they_claim: The cited study measured 231 minutes online daily.
card.the_problem: The measure is smartphone screen time for a defined respondent subset.

claim_quote.original: waren die befragten jungen Menschen 231 Minuten täglich online.
claim_quote.translation_en: Translation: the young people surveyed were online for 231 minutes daily.

request_quote.original: auch junge Menschen an der Erarbeitung des Gesetzes zu beteiligen
request_quote.translation_en: Translation of request fragment: also involve young people in developing the law

counter_quote.original: die tägliche Bildschirmzeit am Smartphone bei 231 Minuten
counter_quote.translation_en: Translation: daily screen time on the smartphone at 231 minutes

additional_counter_quote.original: Auf die Angabe der Onlinezeit wird in der JIM-Studie fortan verzichtet
additional_counter_quote.translation_en: Translation: The JIM study will henceforth omit reporting online time

correction: JIM 2025 reports smartphone screen time, read from the device by respondents able to do so (n=960), rather than total time online across devices. Its methods section explicitly says it stopped reporting unspecific online time. The numeral 231 matches; the measured variable and sample need to be described accurately.
effect: Corrects what the cited usage figure measures. It cannot quantify the total time minors were online or their exposure to digital violence.
limits: Does not establish that actual total online time was above or below 231 minutes: smartphones can be used offline and the internet can be used on other devices. It does not rebut the submission’s separately sourced harassment figures or the case for child-sensitive procedures.
materiality_explanation: Minor: the number is transcribed correctly, while its label and population are broadened. The general case for responding to minors’ needs survives.
direction_explanation: Unknown: the correction does not tell us whether the described online exposure is overstated or understated. Direction is null, although the usage context accompanies explicit requests.
context_and_alternatives: Read the full seven-page submission. The relevant paragraph begins with JIM 2025 and its endnote4 identifies the precise study. It also mentions computer/laptop ownership; no qualification restricts online time to smartphone screen time.
The study summary describes the smartphone as a central device for online applications, which may explain shorthand. Its methods and measure definitions nevertheless distinguish the two variables.
No inference about actual harm from the usage duration is made.

draft.version_evidence: Submission opening states consultation letter17April2026. Compare the April draft, not the later Cabinet text.
draft.relevant_provisions: Article1 procedural protections and disclosure rules; factual study description is independent of later amendments.
